title: Multiplexed Assay for Detection of Cell Culture EV Surface Membrane Proteins
author: Joshua A Welsh
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.be7yjhpw
materials: Determine which antibodies to use to detect EV surface membrane proteins in addition to the included CD9, CD63 and CD81 antibodies. All additional antibodies must be either APC or AF647 conjugated. Ensure you know the concentration of the antibodies, and if you are using an antibody conjugated in-lab, avoid preparations that have unbound dye.
All detection antibodies should be vortexed gently and spun quickly in a table top centrifuge if possible.

Once antibody solutions are prepared, vacuum the plate until the wells are just empty of liquid. Very quickly and gently blot the bottom of the filter plate against a clean paper towel to remove any drops of buffer on the bottom of the plate.
Clear all wells with the vacuum.
Immediately added 150 µL buffer to all wells
Prepare all antibody solutions according to the template spreadsheet. If doing a large experiment make sure to only prepare the antibody solutions immediatley before use.
Use MPA PASS software to analyze the multiplexed EV protein expression data. Protocol under development.

steps.title: Experimental Planning and Calculations
steps.instruction: Determine sample concentrations and plan the plate layout using the MACSplex Protocol Template.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the particle concentration and total particle count of the EV sample.
Use the template to generate a plate map and determine required sample volumes.

Adjust titration points: increase the upper EV titration point for concentrated samples (~5E11 part./mL or greater); concentrate dilute samples if 1E9 EVs cannot be incubated with each detection antibody.
For lower titration points, prepare EV stock dilutions in PBS to use equal volumes across mixes (e.g., 10 µL of 1E11 part/mL and 10 µL of 1E10 part/mL).

Use the 'EV - capture bead mix preparation' section to calculate volumes of MACSplex buffer, MACSplex capture beads, and EVs (combined volume of buffer and EVs in PBS should be 65 µL per 10 µL of beads, or 75 µL per detection antibody 'test').
Use the 'Antibody preparation table' to calculate required volumes of antibodies and buffer for staining.
Identify and record the lot number of the capture bead tube from the digital inventory.

steps.title: Prepare Capture Bead Mixes
steps.instruction: Prepare EV sample collection tubes and incubate EVs with capture beads overnight.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Eppendorf 2.0 mL LoBind collection tubes (or other high-quality low-protein binding tubes).
Transfer the calculated amount of MACSplex buffer to each collection tube.
Spin down and vortex a tube of human MACSPlex Exosome Capture Beads on the highest setting, then aliquot calculated volumes into each sample tube.
Vortex and add the calculated volume of undiluted or diluted EVs to each tube.
Vortex each tube well and place in a tube rotator, covered with foil, rotating overnight at RT. Ensure the volume inverts and falls down the side of the tube to keep beads in suspension.

steps.title: Prepare Filter Plate
steps.instruction: Wet the 0.2 µm PES filter plate to prepare it for sample loading.

substeps.instruction: Obtain a new Pall 0.2 µm PES filter plate.
Using a multichannel pipet, add 150 µL of MACSplex buffer to all sample and control wells.
Subject the plate to vacuum until wells are emptied, release vacuum gently, and quickly blot the bottom of the filter plate against a clean paper towel.
Immediately add 50 µL of MACSplex buffer to the wetted wells.

steps.title: Load Samples and Controls
steps.instruction: Transfer the EV-bead complexes and control beads onto the filter plate.

substeps.instruction: Vortex each EV sample tube thoroughly and add 75 µL (containing 10 µL of capture beads) to each test well.
Add 10 µL of vortexed MACSplex capture beads to the indicated detection antibody control wells (1 per detection antibody).

steps.title: Detection Antibody Staining
steps.instruction: Apply detection antibodies to the captured EVs and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Quickly dispense 200 µL of antibody solution per well using a multichannel pipette to prevent membranes from drying. Ensure equal volumes are drawn and avoid bubbles.
Using a multichannel pipet set to 100 µL, mix the volumes by pipetting up and down. Start in the middle of the fluid and rotate toward the sides; do not scrape or puncture the filter membrane.
Cover the plate with a foil plate sealer and incubate for 2 hours at RT with shaking.

steps.title: Wash and Resuspend Beads
steps.instruction: Wash the captured complexes and resuspend them for flow cytometry analysis.

substeps.instruction: Vacuum the plate until fluid is empty, then immediately add 150 µL of MACSplex buffer to all used wells.
Using a 75 µL setting, reverse pipette all wells (avoiding bubbles and membrane scraping).
Place on vacuum manifold until all wells are cleared.
Immediately add 200 µL of buffer to all wells (this volume can be adjusted for desired final concentration).
Using a 200 µL setting, reverse pipette all wells. When preparing final resuspension, press the multichannel plunger half-way (~100 µL) to fully resuspend beads on the membrane.
Transfer the resuspended beads to Axygen racked mini 1.1 mL tubes or a compatible 96-well plate.

steps.title: Flow Cytometry Analysis
steps.instruction: Calibrate the cytometer and analyze the stained EV samples.

substeps.instruction: Prepare setup beads: add 20 µL of setup beads with 20 µL of PBS to a free well. Also, add 5 µL of capture beads in 200 µL of PBS to another free well.
Run setup beads on the flow cytometer to adjust settings and gate around a single bead population.
Analyze the full volume of each 200 µL stained EV sample, including the non-EV capture bead + detection antibody controls.
